blocks.content: The primary objective of SEBI is to protect the interests of investors in securities and to promote the development of, and to regulate, the securities market.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: SEBI was established to protect the interests of investors in securities and promote the development of the securities market.
The primary objectives are threefold: Investor Protection, Market Regulation, and Market Development.
SEBI aims to prevent malpractices such as insider trading, price rigging, and fraudulent trade practices.
It regulates and registers intermediaries like brokers, sub-brokers, merchant bankers, and portfolio managers.
SEBI provides a platform for issuers to raise capital safely and efficiently.

rows: Protecting investor interests and ensuring fair practices
Prohibiting insider trading, checking price rigging, investor education
Regulating business operations in the stock exchange
Registering brokers, regulating takeover bids, conducting audits
Promoting market activity and adoption of modern practices
Training intermediaries, promoting e-trading, conducting research

items: SEBI received statutory powers on April 12, 1992, through the SEBI Act, 1992.
Questions frequently distinguish between Protective, Regulatory, and Developmental objectives of SEBI.
Prohibition of Insider Trading and Price Rigging comes under SEBI's Protective Functions.
